column11: a scaling to a derived absolute label pool, since the label population sits outside the 7.4mm with Alzheimer's dementia that data/epidemiology.csv carries. By single year of age 55 to 80, the registry's band (NCT06653153): US resident population (Census Bureau Vintage 2024, nc-est2024-agesex-res.csv, 90.85mm aged 55 to 80) x the share neither demented nor with MCI x amyloid positivity among the cognitively normal. Amyloid positivity: 12.9% at 55, 15.8% at 60, 19.2% at 65, 23.1% at 70, 27.6% at 75, 32.6% at 80, interpolated linearly (Jansen et al., JAMA 2015;313(19):1924-38, Table 2, PMID 25988462; the 2022 update, JAMA Neurol 2022;79(3):228-243, PMID 35099509, found prevalence similar to the 2015 estimates). MCI: 6.7% at 60 to 64 (applied from 55), 8.4% at 65 to 69, 10.1% at 70 to 74, 14.8% at 75 to 79, 25.2% at 80 (Petersen et al., Neurology 2018;90(3):126-135, PMID 29282327). Alzheimer's dementia: 5.2% at 65 to 74 and 13.8% at 75 to 84, and 110 per 100,000 below 65 (2026 Alzheimer's Disease Facts and Figures, PMC13098189). Sum: 15.78mm, 17.4% of the age band. 15.78 / 7.4 = 2.1324
column12: the preclinical pool is estimated, not counted: population-based positivity from a meta-analysis of research cohorts, and a plasma p-tau screen will not classify exactly as PET or CSF does. MCI is excluded because the label is no or minimal impairment and MCI patients are already inside Kisunla's label; a trial reading that admits mild MCI would widen the pool. The earlier version used 65 and over at the A4 screening positivity of 29.5% (Sperling et al., JAMA Neurol 2020, PMID 32250387), which included people over 80 whom the trial excludes; it landed within 1% of this figure by offsetting errors

column11: the measured anti-amyloid class new-start rate from CMS Part B beneficiaries. Leqembi (J0174): 961 in 2023 and 7,907 in 2024 (CMS Medicare Part B Spending by Drug, dataset 76a714ad-3a2c-43ac-b76d-9dadf8f7d890) and 14,029 in 2025 (quarterly companion bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)'). Kisunla (J0175): 1,299 in 2024 (drug_demand) and 9,993 in 2025 (quarterly companion). At the 0.333 a year that stays on an 18-month course, 2025 new starts are 14,029 - 7,907 x 0.333 = 11,396 and 9,993 - 1,299 x 0.333 = 9,560, 20,956 together, 0.954% of the 2,197,800 symptomatic label pool the trontinemab seed carries (Dittrich et al., Neurology 2024). A 0.5x multiple gives 0.477%
column12: the 0.5x is a judgement and the most arguable figure here. No drug treats preclinical Alzheimer's, and people without symptoms rarely see a clinician who would test them. On the 15.78mm pool 0.477% is about 75,000 US starts a year at peak, 3.6 times the whole class's 2025 starts. The case for higher: home injection removes the infusion chair, and plasma p-tau testing is cheap. The case for lower: ARIA MRI monitoring and CMS coverage with evidence development still apply to the class, and payers may resist treating people without symptoms
